"title": "QED⊗QCD Resummation and Shower/ME Matching for LHC Physics",
"authors": "B.F.L. Ward and S.A. Yost",
"field_subfield": "High-energy particle physics (QCD resummation / precision LHC phenomenology)",
"type_of_paper": "Theory paper (analytical resummation framework with semi-analytical and planned Monte Carlo applications)",
"executive_summary": "This paper develops a theory of QED⊗QCD resummation and its interplay with parton-shower/matrix-element matching for precision LHC physics. The motivation is the luminosity measurement at the LHC, which requires a theoretical precision tag at the 0.67% level for processes such as single W and Z boson production decaying to light leptons, so as not to compromise the overall luminosity determination at the ~2% experimental precision. To meet this, multiple gluon and photon radiative effects must be controlled, which the theory of QED⊗QCD exponentiation allows by simultaneously resumming multiple gluon and photon radiation to all orders in both αs and α without double-counting effects. The authors build on the QCD resummation theory of Ref. [3], which is an exact rearrangement of the QCD perturbative series based on the N = 1 term in the exponent in the formal proof of exponentiation in non-Abelian gauge theories in the eikonal approximation (Ref. [4]). This exponential is augmented with a sum of residuals that account for the remaining contributions to the perturbative series exactly to all orders in αs, giving an exact result, whereas the resummation theories in Refs. [4, 5–7] are approximate. The extension to QED⊗QCD is obtained by simultaneously exponentiating the large infrared terms in QCD and the exact infrared-divergent terms in QED, using new YFS residuals that represent the successive application of the YFS expansion first for QCD and then for QED. The infrared algebra implies that QCD-dominant corrections occur about an order of magnitude earlier than QED corrections, so the leading residual level already gives a good estimate of the interplay between higher-order QED and QCD effects. The authors apply the theory to heavy gauge boson production, computing the ratio of the exponentiated cross section to the Born cross section, rexp = σexp/σBorn, at both the LHC and the Tevatron, with and without QED. They find that QED effects are at the ~0.3% level at both colliders, stable under scale variations, and similar in size to structure-function results found in the literature. They also discuss how to combine the exact YFS-style resummation calculus with HERWIG and/or PYTHIA parton showers using pT matching, and describe a more accurate shower-subtracted residual approach. The semi-analytical results for QED (and QCD) threshold effects agree with the literature on Z production, and the full Monte Carlo event generator realization is possible in principle. The corresponding analysis of W production is in progress. The paper provides a firm theoretical basis for the realization of the complete O(α2s, ααs, α2) results needed for FNAL/LHC/RHIC/ILC physics.",

summary.title: QED⊗QCD Resummation and Shower/ME Matching for LHC Physics
summary.field_subfield: High-energy particle physics (QCD resummation / precision LHC phenomenology)
summary.type_of_paper: Theory paper (analytical resummation framework with semi-analytical and planned Monte Carlo applications)
summary.executive_summary: This paper develops a theory of QED⊗QCD resummation and its interplay with parton-shower/matrix-element matching for precision LHC physics. The motivation is the luminosity measurement at the LHC, which requires a theoretical precision tag at the 0.67% level for processes such as single W and Z boson production decaying to light leptons, so as not to compromise the overall luminosity determination at the ~2% experimental precision. To meet this, multiple gluon and photon radiative effects must be controlled, which the theory of QED⊗QCD exponentiation allows by simultaneously resumming multiple gluon and photon radiation to all orders in both αs and α without double-counting effects. The authors build on the QCD resummation theory of Ref. [3], which is an exact rearrangement of the QCD perturbative series based on the N = 1 term in the exponent in the formal proof of exponentiation in non-Abelian gauge theories in the eikonal approximation (Ref. [4]). This exponential is augmented with a sum of residuals that account for the remaining contributions to the perturbative series exactly to all orders in αs, giving an exact result, whereas the resummation theories in Refs. [4, 5–7] are approximate. The extension to QED⊗QCD is obtained by simultaneously exponentiating the large infrared terms in QCD and the exact infrared-divergent terms in QED, using new YFS residuals that represent the successive application of the YFS expansion first for QCD and then for QED. The infrared algebra implies that QCD-dominant corrections occur about an order of magnitude earlier than QED corrections, so the leading residual level already gives a good estimate of the interplay between higher-order QED and QCD effects. The authors apply the theory to heavy gauge boson production, computing the ratio of the exponentiated cross section to the Born cross section, rexp = σexp/σBorn, at both the LHC and the Tevatron, with and without QED. They find that QED effects are at the ~0.3% level at both colliders, stable under scale variations, and similar in size to structure-function results found in the literature. They also discuss how to combine the exact YFS-style resummation calculus with HERWIG and/or PYTHIA parton showers using pT matching, and describe a more accurate shower-subtracted residual approach. The semi-analytical results for QED (and QCD) threshold effects agree with the literature on Z production, and the full Monte Carlo event generator realization is possible in principle. The corresponding analysis of W production is in progress. The paper provides a firm theoretical basis for the realization of the complete O(α2s, ααs, α2) results needed for FNAL/LHC/RHIC/ILC physics.
